clue.text: US writer Henry Marie describes ferns on hill crest

parts.note: bracken is a common coarse fern of hillsides
a ridge is the long crest along the top of a hill

explanation.surface: A naturalist's description of ferns growing on the crest of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Marie Brackenridge (1786-1871) was an American writer and traveller; 'describes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name identifies the American author and son of the novelist Hugh Henry Brackenridge.

clue.text: Abbot and saint — lop both into pieces for travellers' friend

indicators.note: breaking the words into pieces signals that their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A violent instruction to chop both things up, with a holy man somehow in the frame.
explanation.walkthrough: St Botolph, a seventh-century English abbot, is patron saint of travellers, hence 'travellers' friend', which adds to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh-century East Anglian holy man founded a monastery and was later venerated, so he was both monastic head and saint.

clue.text: Declares a curtailed poem

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: a verse is a poem or piece of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone announces a poem that has been cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver something is to state it firmly, a direct synonym of declaring.

clue.text: She married One Gentleman of Verona

definitions.text: She married One Gentleman of Verona

parts.words: She married One Gentleman of Verona
parts.note: the shrew of Shakespeare's comedy weds Petruchio, a gentleman of Verona, playing on the title of The Two Gentlemen of Verona

explanation.surface: A bride wed one of Shakespeare's two Veronese gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The title points to The Two Gentlemen of Verona, but the husband is Petruchio of The Taming of the Shrew, who calls himself a gentleman of Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Petruchio's bride in The Taming of the Shrew is the shrew herself, Baptista's elder daughter.

clue.text: Woman driver employed by Zeus

parts.note: the winged Greek goddess of victory was said to drive the chariot of the king of the gods

explanation.surface: A female chauffeur on the payroll of the chief god.
explanation.definitionFit: The goddess of victory served as charioteer to Zeus in Greek myth.

clue.text: "A strong ass", according to his father, "couching down between two burdens"

definitions.text: "A strong ass", according to his father, "couching down between two burdens"

parts.words: "A strong ass", according to his father, "couching down between two burdens"
parts.note: Jacob's blessing of his sons in Genesis 49:14 describes one son with exactly these words

explanation.surface: A father's unflattering description of his son as a beast of burden.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis 49 Jacob blesses this son, the ninth, as a strong donkey lying between two loads.

clue.text: Berlin theatre maximised by Russian dramatist

definitions.text: Berlin theatre maximised by Russian dramatist

parts.words: Berlin theatre maximised by Russian dramatist
parts.note: a Berlin playhouse is named after Maxim, the Russian writer, so it has been 'Maxim-ised' by him

explanation.surface: A Berlin theatre greatly expanded by a Russian playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maximised' looks like 'enlarged', but it means given the first name Maxim: Berlin's Maxim Gorki Theater.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorky (also spelt Gorki) was a Russian playwright, author of The Lower Depths.

clue.text: Like the teaching of Torah in BBC air broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A religious programme on Torah teaching aired by the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Torah teaching is the work of rabbis, so it is of or relating to rabbis.

clue.text: Second of two writers identifying Thackeray's work

definitions.text: Second of two writers identifying Thackeray's work

parts.words: Second of two writers identifying Thackeray's work
parts.note: the title of Thackeray's novel ... splits into PEN, a writer, followed by the name of the critic John ..., also a writer

explanation.surface: A clue to the second author named in a Thackeray title.
explanation.walkthrough: Pendennis = PEN (a writer) + the surname of John Dennis, the eighteenth-century critic.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dennis was an English critic and playwright whose surname completes the title of Thackeray's novel.

clue.text: Our Lady of Vladimir, an iconic concept

definitions.text: Our Lady of Vladimir, an iconic concept

parts.words: Our Lady of Vladimir, an iconic concept
parts.note: the famous Russian icon portrays the Virgin as God-bearer, the Greek title for Mary

explanation.surface: Describing the famous Russian icon of the Virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iconic' is literal: the Vladimir Mother of God is an icon, and 'concept' plays on conception, the bearing of God.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek title means 'God-bearer', the Orthodox name for the Virgin Mary depicted in that icon.

clue.text: Where a deceitful fellow conceals a writer

indicators.note: the fellow's words conceal the writer's name within their letters

explanation.surface: Asking where a liar hides a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'wheRE A DEceitful'. Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was an English novelist and dramatist of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Perelman suggested thus paying attention to a mimic

definitions.text: Perelman suggested thus paying attention to a mimic

parts.words: Perelman suggested thus paying attention to a mimic
parts.note: S. J. Perelman's book ... to the Mocking Bird urges attention to a bird famous as a mimic

explanation.surface: The American humorist recommended heeding an impressionist.
explanation.walkthrough: A mockingbird copies other birds' songs, so 'a mimic' stands for it in Perelman's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title's first word is an imperative meaning to attend with the ears.

clue.text: Cabin, sir? Possibly, for Russian

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A steward asks a passenger whether he wants a cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Scriabin was a Russian composer and pianist.

clue.text: Potter's companion in Williams leitmotif

parts.note: Harry Potter's snowy owl gives her name to the main theme John Williams wrote for the films

explanation.surface: A potter's friend appears in a recurring musical theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' is Harry Potter, not a maker of pots; the film theme is Hedwig's Theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry's pet owl is his constant companion, and John Williams's score is named after her.

clue.text: Allotted sides long locked in floral rivalry

definitions.text: Allotted sides long locked in floral rivalry

parts.words: Allotted sides long locked in floral rivalry
parts.note: the Wars of the Roses were fought between the houses holding the titles of York and Lancaster

explanation.surface: Two teams locked in a long competition between flower growers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floral rivalry' is the Wars of the Roses (white rose of York, red rose of Lancaster); the sides are noble titles with their lands.
explanation.definitionFit: York and Lancaster were noble titles held by royal princes, each with its territory.

clue.text: Christie's detective friend from Sussex town

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's sidekick comes from the south coast of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Hastings is Poirot's friend and narrator; Hastings is a town in East Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Poirot's companion Captain Arthur shares his surname with the seaside town famous for the battle of 1066.

clue.text: Noble, if Machiavellian theme

explanation.surface: A noble subject, if a scheming one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Machiavellian' looks like 'scheming' but points to Machiavelli's treatise Il Principe.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal son is a noble of the highest rank, and Machiavelli's famous treatise on rule bears that title.

clue.text: Rio samba possibly offering source of everlasting life

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Carnival dancing in Brazil offers immortal bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the food of the gods conferred immortality on those who ate it.

clue.text: Action suggested by Hamlet to oppose a large number of difficulties

definitions.text: Action suggested by Hamlet to oppose a large number of difficulties

parts.words: Action suggested by Hamlet to oppose a large number of difficulties
parts.note: in the 'To be or not to be' speech Hamlet weighs taking up weapons against a sea of troubles

explanation.surface: Hamlet's advice for facing a heap of problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The soliloquy asks whether it is nobler to suffer, 'Or to take arms against a sea of troubles'; 'a large number of difficulties' is the sea of troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's line names the act of picking up weapons to fight, here against troubles.

clue.text: Quotation source from Indian writer

parts.note: a tag is a familiar quotation or saying
ore is the rock that is the source of metal

explanation.surface: Tracing a quotation back to its Indian author.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet and Nobel laureate in literature.

clue.text: Henley's Brodie with Stevenson

parts.note: W. E. Henley and R. L. Stevenson co-wrote a play about the Edinburgh cabinet-maker by day, burglar by night, William Brodie

explanation.surface: A play by Henley written jointly with Stevenson.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is Deacon Brodie, or The Double Life (1880); William Brodie was a deacon of the Edinburgh trades guild.
explanation.definitionFit: The real Brodie held the title of deacon, head of his trade guild, which named the play.

clue.text: Barrister's clerk for Belmont lady richly left "

definitions.text: Barrister's clerk for Belmont lady richly left

parts.words: Barrister's clerk for Belmont lady richly left
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice Portia's maid disguises herself as the clerk of Portia's lawyer persona

explanation.surface: A legal clerk working for a wealthy heiress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Belmont is a lady richly left' is Bassanio's description of Portia; her waiting-woman plays the clerk to Portia's disguised lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia's waiting-woman in The Merchant of Venice poses as a lawyer's clerk at the trial.

clue.text: Longfellow's burial-ground

parts.note: Longfellow's poem calls a churchyard by an old Saxon phrase meaning the field of the Lord

explanation.surface: The cemetery where an American poet is buried.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like Longfellow's grave, but it is the title of his poem 'God's-Acre', an old name for a churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a churchyard, used as the title of Longfellow's poem.

clue.text: Russell child is Argonaut's father

parts.note: the Irish poet George William Russell wrote under the pen name AE
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: One of the Russells has a son who sails with Jason.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Aeson was the father of Jason, leader of the Argonauts.

clue.text: Bowman of Henry Irving

explanation.surface: An archer in the company of the great Victorian actor.
explanation.walkthrough: William Archer, the critic, wrote a study of the actor Henry Irving, so the book is 'Henry Irving' by him.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman shoots with a bow, and the critic William Archer was author of a book on the actor.

clue.text: Pilgrim seen in verse of fresh ad jingle

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the words of the advertising verse

explanation.surface: A pilgrim appears in the lines of a new advertising jingle.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is 'fresH AD JIngle'. A hadji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is given to a Muslim who has completed the hajj to Mecca.

clue.text: Mame (musical) adapted from this book?

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of the musical's name are reworked into another form

explanation.surface: Asking whether the musical Mame was adapted from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's novel's title is the musical's name rearranged; '(musical)' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel of 1815 is a famous book of that title.

clue.text: Frost's are, with costs

parts.note: the word Frost's rhymes with costs, and frosts are also hoar frosts, so both readings point to the same word

explanation.surface: Robert Frost's verses compared with prices.
explanation.walkthrough: Old spelling of rhymes: 'Frost's' rhymes with 'costs', and in the other sense frosts are rime.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic spelling of rhymes doubles as the plural of rime, a feathery hoar frost.

clue.text: Greek poet has a date in Rome with simple chap

parts.note: Simple Simon is the foolish chap of the nursery rhyme
the Ides was a fixed date in the Roman calendar, mid-month

explanation.surface: A Greek poet goes on a date in Rome with a simpleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Simonides of Ceos was a Greek lyric poet of the sixth and fifth centuries BC.

clue.text: Nina and Karen with articles about tragic heroine

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an and a are the indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Two women named Nina and Karen are accompanied by some written pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the letters of NINA, KAREN, AN and A into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's heroine throws herself under a train, a classic tragic ending.
